text:
Ava: Hey team — customer reports a sudden flurry of 429s even though their dashboard shows non-zero burst credits. Happening after a recent traffic spike, they say requests were ~12 concurrent workers.
Ben: Can you paste the raw 429 response headers? usually X-Burst-Credits and Retry-After tell us what's up.
Ava: Pasting from their logs: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 120
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-Burst-Credits: 0
Retry-After: 3
Date: Tue, 09 Mar 2026 21:10:05 GMT
```
They also included an earlier snapshot showing X-Burst-Credits: 2 then quickly to 0.
Chandra: A few possibilities: (1) burst credits drained quickly due to many short-lived parallel requests, (2) per-route smoothing policy may be rebalancing credits across tokens and causing transient 429s, or (3) a sticky routing mismatch to a capacity-constrained pool.
Ava: Customer repro steps: 
1) Start 12 workers, each does: 
```
while true; do curl -sS -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -d '{"model":"rdx-large-v1","input":"summarize ..."}'; sleep 0.1; done
```
2) After ~90s they see 429 spikes across all workers.
Ben: That script is high concurrency + short sleep — favorite pattern to blow through credits. Also, small per-request payloads increase token-rate inefficiency.
SupportSRE: InfraBot ran a quick check on the customer's route: 
```
InfraBot: route=customer-A-prod pool=shared-usw2_1 concurrent_open=96
InfraBot: burst_window_ms=60000 refill_rate_per_min=30 per_route_quota=120/min
InfraBot: recent_token_rate_spike=+8x over baseline
```
Chandra: Looks like the shared pool was receiving a big burst. The burst_window is 60s and refill_rate is small, so credits are exhausted quickly. Also we saw many parallel connections which defeats smoothing.
Ava: Customer asked why dashboard shows some credits earlier but still 429s later — they think it's a UI bug.
Ben: Not a UI bug: credits are consumed and then refilled slowly. Dashboards are eventual. Also note we have two credit axes: per-customer burst credits and per-route smoothing buckets. If the route gets overloaded, router will serve 429s even if customer-wide credits exist but are already assigned to other concurrent tokens.
Ava: What quick mitigations can we give the customer for today?
Chandra: Short-term: 1) Reduce client concurrency to 4 (max). 2) Add jittered exponential backoff honoring Retry-After header. 3) Increase request batching to reduce per-request overhead (combine multiple prompts). 4) If possible, pin the route to Dedicated or increase quota temporarily.
Ben: Add this sample SDK pseudo-config they can use immediately: 
```
client.configure({
  maxConcurrency: 4,
  retry: { retries: 6, factor: 2, minTimeoutMs: 500, jitter: true },
  batchSize: 4
});
```
Ava: I sent those suggestions. Customer tried maxConcurrency=4 + backoff and saw 429s drop substantially within 2 minutes.
SupportSRE: Follow-ups for us: 
- Check whether per-route smoothing assignment caused asymmetric drain across tokens (assign to @Chandra)
- Evaluate temporary bump of refill_rate_per_min for the route (assign to @Ben)
- Coordinate with billing if customer requests partial burst credit refund (assign to @Ava)
Chandra: Quick infra findings: the router's bucket allocation was LIFO during the spike which made hot tokens get drained. We'll flip to fair-share allocation in the next patch; small risk but should reduce simultaneous 429s.
Ben: I created a short-lived policy to increase refill_rate_per_min to 120 for 15 minutes on customer-A-prod — applied at 21:12 UTC and we saw error rate drop from 8% -> 0.8% by 21:16.
Ava: Customer confirmed improved behavior and asked for guidance on long-term config. I recommended: 
- Use Dedicated for steady high-concurrency workloads.
- Tune batching and client-side concurrency.
- Use longer smoothing window (e.g., 120000 ms) if their traffic is bursty but sustained.
Chandra: Note on smoothing window trade-offs: longer window = smoother experience for frequent spikes, but increases tail latency for sudden single-request bursts. Recommend testing with 60s -> 120s incrementally.
SupportSRE: Billing note: create a manual credit for 10% of the burst consumption while we investigate router behavior. @Ava can you open a billing ticket?
Ava: Opened billing ticket #BILL-1298 and cc'd the customer.
Ben: I'll roll the fair-share allocation patch to canary tonight and monitor.
Ava: Closing loop with customer — they scheduled a follow-up for tomorrow to discuss Dedicated vs shared optimizations. Marking this thread resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
SupportSRE: Logging action items in ops-runbook: "burst-credit - transient 429 triage" and linking this thread.
